title: KV cache microsegregation smoothing and reclamation playbook
creator: Priya Patel
description: Objective: Reduce long-term GPU memory fragmentation caused by continuous batching and KV cache growth while preserving low tail latency. Deliver a low-risk, incremental reclamation strategy (microsegregation + smoothing windows + fast background migration) that interoperates with our batching runtime and existing slab pools. Goals: 1) Keep median generation latency unchanged; 2) Reduce fraction of OOMs and forced evictions due to fragmentation by >= 60% on synthetic mixed workloads; 3) Limit extra CPU/GPU copy overhead to < 6% of token-serving cost under steady-state workloads. Scope: - Allocation strategy: introduce microsegregation bins (microzones) inside existing slab pools to limit intra-slab fragmentation for variable-length KV entries. - Smoothing: apply time-decayed smoothing windows to reasoning about hot/cold split so small transient hot bursts from continuous batching don't force compaction. - Reclamation: background incremental migration (small-chunk relocation) and on-demand local compaction triggered by fragmentation watermarks; avoid global stop-the-world compaction. - Integration: hook allocator signals into continuous batching controller so batch planner can avoid packing hot mutable prefixes into shared microzones during compaction. - Telemetry: new metrics and dashboards for microzone occupancy, relocation throughput, fragmentation ratio by slab, eviction-triggered compactions, and per-customer fragmentation incidents. Acceptance criteria: - Implementation passes benchmarks for 3 representative workloads (short chat, long-context summarization, mixed interactive batch) with fragmentation incidents reduced per goal above. - No more than 2% increase in P99 latency on steady-state tests. - Feature gated with config flags and rollout plan for dedicated clusters before hosted rollout. Implementation outline: 1) Microsegregation allocator: create microzones sized at power-of-two granularity but with small microzone buckets for common KV sizes (e.g., 32B, 128B, 512B, 4KB). Each microzone is a sub-slab with local freelist and soft-reserve watermark. 2) Smoothing windows: maintain short time window (configurable, default 10s) that smooths hotness signals; entries must be hot-stable before being promoted to hot partitions. This prevents continuous batching spikes from causing churn. 3) Reclamation strategy: two-tier reclamation: - Passive: opportunistic coalescing during background eviction windows when GPU is underutilized (low GPU utilization or inter-request gaps). - Active incremental relocate: move residents in small chunks (e.g., 8KB copy quanta) to free microzones; prioritize cold-origin entries. Migration is throttled by per-device budget to cap overhead. 4) Eviction hysteresis and backoff: add retention hysteresis that increases with relocation failures to avoid repeated churn. 5) Integration with batching: batch planner exposes predicted prefix-stability flag; allocator can temporarily avoid placing stable prefixes into reclaimable microzones. 6) Telemetry & tracing: emit relocation trace events with request ids, microzone id, copy bytes, and latency impact for each relocation. Rollout plan: - Phase 0: Feature branch + unit tests + allocator simulation harness (local). - Phase 1: Canary on internal dedicated cluster with synthetic workloads; collect fragmentation and latency metrics for 48h. - Phase 2: Opt-in beta for select customers on dedicated offering. - Phase 3: Gradual ramp to hosted API with kill-switch and auto-fallback to current allocator. Observability: dashboards to add: microzone-occupancy, fragmentation-heatmap (per-GPU), relocate-throughput, eviction-hysteresis-events, customer-fragmentation-incidents. Links: design doc (confluence) - https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RW/kv-microsegregation-design, allocator sim repo - https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-allocator-sim, initial PR - https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2891. Risks & mitigations: - Risk: Background relocation competes with token serving and increases tail latency. Mitigation: enforce strict relocation throttles tied to GPU utilization and prioritize token-serving streams; use GPU async copy queues. - Risk: Hot/cold misclassification leading to oscillation. Mitigation: smoothing windows + promotion/demotion cooldown + dynamic thresholds. - Risk: Increased complexity and maintainability burden. Mitigation: keep core allocator primitives minimal and encapsulate microzone policy behind a flag and clear API; extensive unit/integration tests. Open questions: - What default microzone size distribution yields best trade-off across workloads? (action: run large-scale sim) - How to set relocation budgets per-GPU dynamically across mixed-tenancy? (action: prototype autoscaler for relocation budgets) - Interplay with quantized models using different KV footprints (action: add quantized-aware size buckets).
